evidence_boundary: Local integration evidence of upstream native operations: every fixture runs the pinned tool's own CLI or MCP commands and this repository's checks assert on what they return. The one upstream test in the harness is rtk verify --require-all, the inline tests of RTK's built-in TOML filters shipped in its release binary (154 of 154 passed in each run below). No other pinned tool documents an offline self-test command (upstream_self_test_survey). Upstream test-suite qualification of a component belongs in its per-host receipts, evidence/hosts/<host>/<host>--<component>--<stage>--<date>.json, recorded with scripts/host_receipts.py and summarized in docs/component-evidence-matrix.md; the receipts recorded so far for these eleven tools run install and use commands, not upstream suites.

final_runs.note: Two consecutive --install runs of the final harness, after the GPT-6 repair round. This round could write only inside the checkout and one session scratch directory, whose path is long, so TMPDIR was a new directory inside it. codebase-memory-mcp's rendezvous socket would then not fit a Unix socket address (with a 4-digit uid, TMPDIR may be at most 36 bytes), and the harness's own require_cbm_socket_fits refused that fixture, as designed, after installation and the --version check but before any other codebase-memory-mcp command. Every other check passed. The codebase-memory-mcp fixture therefore last ran in the pre_polish_runs below; see codebase_memory_fixture_unchanged.

host_default_headroom_workspace_observat.note: The controls driver never wrote there: each of its runs, the polish pass's three and this round's two, went through clean_env_run.sh with a throwaway HOME (the first at 06:50:13Z), and nothing under ~/.headroom changed after 02:33:08Z. No file there was created by this change, so none was removed. The first draft's six --install runs that reached Headroom (01:51 to 02:32Z) had no HEADROOM_WORKSPACE_DIR and kept the native HOME (draft_runs_with_account_default_cbm_state), and the store and session stats were last modified at 02:32:52Z, during the last of them; those draft runs most likely added entries to these pre-existing files. The files belong to the workstation's own Headroom and were left unchanged.

pre_polish_runs.note: The port's two passing --install runs of the pre-polish harness, 89 commands and 36 of 36 checks each, codebase-memory-mcp included, with TMPDIR unset (/tmp). That harness wrote source hashes as a map keyed by file path, a shape gitleaks' generic-api-key rule reports under the repository's .gitleaks.toml (two findings per receipt). The committed receipts hold the same entries as the source_files list of {path, sha256} objects that the final harness writes itself, at the same position; nothing else differs. tests/test_native_token_ci.py rebuilds the map and checks private_original_sha256.

superseded_runs.note: Same wrapper and invocation, earlier harness revision: both passed, but their receipts retained the run-owned directory home/jcodemunch-mcp under <WORK>, a shape the repository's publication scan (scripts/validate.py PRIVATE_CONTENT) rejects as a personal home path. The directory is now jcodemunch-mcp-home, with a regression test; the pre-polish and final runs use it. These receipts also used the renamed archive key described in the third entry.

Same wrapper and invocation, with harness ab722d78, which had also renamed rtk_archive_sha256 (see the third entry), not the final pre-polish harness 3cec918f: both passed, but the checkout still carried the first draft's timeout-minutes 20 -> 30 edit to .github/workflows/native-token-e2e.yml, whose bytes tests/test_workflow_hardening.py pins to retained evidence. The edit was reverted, so these receipts record a workflow hash that is not committed.

Same wrapper and invocation, with the committed workflow: both passed, but that harness had renamed the report key rtk_archive_sha256, which the retained reproduction evidence/artifacts/sota-refresh-20260925/rtk/native_token_ci_rtk_only.py reads, so a rerun of it printed no archive hash. Each release-tarball tool now keeps its own <name>_archive_sha256 key, with a regression test. During the second of these runs the account-default rendezvous lost the workstation daemon's endpoint entries (.anc, .sock, .sock.identity): that daemon, from the workstation's own installation and started at 05:01:09Z, had exited by 05:20:55Z, as had a frontend of the same installation that appeared with it; neither belonged to the run.
